departs_from_idea: idea.md asks for 2 sessions; this spec plans 3. 11 cut points and 17 criteria do not fit two sessions under the house caps of 5 cuts and 6 criteria per session, and session 3 is the idea's stated payoff.

idea.md scope bullet 1 says the JSON file is read and written through route handlers, while idea.md out-of-scope bullet 1 rules out adding, editing and deleting bills. This spec follows the out-of-scope list: the store is read-only and there is no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE handler.
notes.data_file: data/bills.json holds an array of 6 Bill objects in the order listed below, newest date first.

types.Bill: { id: string; place: string; date: string; totalPaise: number; tipPercent: number; people: number }

money.unit: Every amount is a whole number of paise. No amount is held as a rupee value with a decimal point.
money.formatRupees: SHIPS WRITTEN in lib/money.ts, not a cut point. formatRupees(paise) returns the character rupee sign, then Math.floor(paise / 100), then a full stop, then paise % 100 padded to two digits. 124000 prints as the rupee sign followed by 1240.00. No thousands separators.
money.tipPaise: lib/money.ts. tipPaise(totalPaise, tipPercent) = Math.floor((totalPaise * tipPercent + 50) / 100), which is half-up rounding on whole paise. Body is cut-money-tip.
money.grandTotal: SHIPS WRITTEN in app/bills/[id]/BillView.tsx, outside every cut: const grandTotalPaise = bill.totalPaise + tipPaise(bill.totalPaise, bill.tipPercent)
money.splitPaise: lib/money.ts. splitPaise(amountPaise, people) returns one share per person in person order; each share is Math.floor(amountPaise / people) and the first amountPaise % people people get one extra paisa each, so the shares sum to amountPaise exactly. Body is cut-money-split.
money.no_zero_tip: No seed bill has a tipPercent of 0, because a tip of zero is what the unfilled cut-money-tip block produces.

store.exports: readAllBills(): Bill[] and findBill(id: string): Bill | null, and no others. Both read data/bills.json on every call. Neither writes.

skeleton_rules: A cut is a block inside a function and the code around it compiles while the block is a hint comment. Where a block produces a value the code below reads, the variable is declared above the opening marker and the block assigns to it: cut-list-cards assigns to a ReactNode[] declared above the marker, cut-bill-shares assigns to the shares array declared above its marker.

A cut that would otherwise remove its function's only return keeps a typed fallback return outside the markers, as the last statement: return bills after let bills: Bill[] = [] in readAllBills, return bill after let bill: Bill | null = null in findBill, return tip after let tip = 0 in tipPaise, return shares after let shares: number[] = [] in splitPaise, and NextResponse.json({ error: 'not implemented' }, { status: 501 }) in each of the two route handlers. 501 belongs to the skeleton alone; the finished project answers only the statuses in the endpoints table.

Each fallback fails the criteria it should: return [] in readAllBills fails c-1-1; 501 fails every endpoint criterion; tip = 0 makes bill-tip-amount read the rupee sign followed by 0.00 and makes bill-grand-total equal bill-total, failing c-2-4 and c-2-6 while leaving c-2-3 green on the stored total; shares = [] renders no share-row, failing every session-3 criterion that counts one; a setPeopleClamped that does nothing leaves people-count on the stored value, failing c-3-2, c-3-5 and c-3-6.
Each cut id appears exactly once in the final code, between its markers.
notes.criterion_cuts_convention: A criterion lists every cut whose block must be filled for its assertion to hold, cuts from earlier sessions included. A cut whose block the criterion renders but does not assert on is not listed: c-3-6 reads only people-count, so it does not list cut-money-split.
notes.subset_satisfied_criteria: c-2-2 and c-2-5 both assert the 404 path, and findBill's typed fallback is return null, which is the same answer a real miss gives. Both go green with cut-store-read-all and cut-store-find-one still open. Bill | null admits no other typed fallback. Pair c-2-2 with c-2-1 and c-2-5 with c-2-3 in any per-cut checkpoint; never present either alone. No other criterion in this spec is satisfied by a proper subset of its cuts.
notes.uncovered_states: The loading state of both screens carries no criterion on purpose: it is what a skeleton shows while its fetch cut is open, so a criterion asserting it would be green on an empty skeleton. It is covered indirectly, because every criterion that reads a card, a bill field or a share row can only pass once its screen has left loading.

endpoints.response: Bill[] - all 6 seed bills, whole Bill objects, in the order data/bills.json stores them
Bill on 200; a JSON body holding an error field on 404

elements: loading message reading Loading saved bills, written outside every cut
grid of bill-card elements, one per bill, in the order the endpoint returns them
bill-card: a link to /bills/<id> holding card-place, card-date, card-total and card-people
card-people reads the word Split, the stored people count, then the word ways
screens.state_shape: app/page.tsx is a client component holding bills: Bill[] starting at [] and status: 'loading' | 'loaded' starting at 'loading', both declared outside every cut. cut-list-fetch is the only code that moves status, and it moves it to 'loaded' only on a 200 reply. There is no empty state: the store always holds 6 bills and nothing filters the list.
screens.fetch_owner: The useEffect call and its empty dependency array [] ship written; cut-list-fetch is the body of that effect. It is the only fetch on this screen.

elements: bill-total, bill-tip-percent reading the percentage and a percent sign, bill-tip-amount and bill-grand-total
bill-saved-people reading Split 4 ways when saved for a bill stored as split 4 ways

people stepper: a minus control with the accessible name Fewer people, the people-count element, a plus control with the accessible name More people; both stay clickable at every count because the clamp lives in the state setter, not in a disabled attribute

heading reading What each person owes, and one share-row per entry of shares, in order, each reading the word Person, the position counting from 1, a space, then formatRupees of that share; this rendering ships written
back link with the accessible name Back to saved bills, to /
loading message reading Loading bill, written outside every cut
not-found message reading Bill not found, shown with the back link, written outside every cut
screens.state_shape: app/bills/[id]/page.tsx holds bill: Bill | null starting at null and status: 'loading' | 'loaded' | 'not-found' starting at 'loading', both outside every cut; cut-bill-fetch is the only code that moves status, and a reply that is neither 200 nor 404 leaves it on 'loading'. app/bills/[id]/BillView.tsx holds people: number starting at bill.people, outside every cut; the minus and plus controls call setPeopleClamped(people - 1) and setPeopleClamped(people + 1), both written outside every cut, and cut-bill-people is the body of setPeopleClamped. BillView mounts only in the loaded state, so bill is never null when the initial people value is read.
screens.fetch_owner: The id comes from useParams; the useEffect call and its dependency array [id] ship written; cut-bill-fetch is the body of that effect. It is the only fetch on this screen.
screens.derived: BillView computes on every render: grandTotalPaise ships written, then let shares: number[] = [] is declared and cut-bill-shares assigns to it. shares is rebuilt from the fetched bill and the current people on every render, never from what is on screen, so 4 to 3 to 4 lands back on the stored split.
screens.inert_until_session_3: sc-bill is built in session 2 and the stepper and the share list are in the file from session 2. Until cut-bill-people is filled the stepper is inert and people-count stays on the stored count. Until cut-money-split and cut-bill-shares are filled, shares stays [] and no share-row is rendered. No session-2 criterion reads people-count or a share-row.

sessions.goal: Serve every saved bill from the JSON store through a route handler and render one card per bill on the list screen.

reading a JSON file on the server with node fs
typing a response with a shared TypeScript type
fetching into React state with useEffect
rendering a list with map and keys
printing an integer paise amount as rupees

sessions.title: One bill, tip included

returning 404 with a JSON body from a route handler
reading the route id with useParams
branching on the response status in a client component
percentage arithmetic on integers with half-up rounding, so money never touches a float

cuts.hint: Put the bill whose id matches the one asked for into the value this function returns, leaving it null when the store holds no bill with that id.
Reply with the bill as JSON and status 200 when the store finds it, and with status 404 and a JSON body holding an error field when the store finds nothing.
Ask the endpoint for the bill named in the route; on a 200 reply put the bill into state and move the status to loaded, and on a 404 reply move the status to not-found.

Work out the tip as the total times the tip percentage divided by a hundred, rounded half up, and put it into the whole-paise number this function returns, without turning any value into rupees along the way.

sessions.title: Re-split the bill
sessions.goal: Compute what each person owes from the people count held in React state, so the shares on screen always add back up to the total with tip.
teaches: deriving what is on screen from state instead of from the server
integer division and remainder as a way to split money without losing a paisa
handing the leftover paise to the first people in the list
clamping a value inside a state setter
recomputing from the stored bill on every render rather than from what is on screen

cuts.hint: Fill the array this function returns with one share per person: give every person the amount divided by the number of people ignoring the remainder, then give one extra paisa each to as many people from the start of the list as there are paise left over.
Work out what each person owes by splitting the total with tip across the number of people currently held in state, and assign that array of shares to the shares variable declared above.
